findings.passage: The SAVE Act, Senate Bill 986, which I have proudly filed again this year, builds directly on this voter-approved constitutional foundation and the broader national momentum for secure elections.
findings.note: Senate release in his name: he refiled SB 986 and ties it to the 2024 constitutional amendment limiting voting to citizens.

findings.passage: It requires applicants to provide clear documentary proof of citizenship—helping to confirm elections are conducted fairly, securely and with the integrity that Americans expect and deserve.
findings.note: Describes what SB 986 requires of people registering to vote.

findings.passage: Election interference can come in many forms.
findings.note: Opening line of his argument for SB 896, a bill limiting outside money and in-kind help for election administration.

findings.passage: The legislation is a straightforward, commonsense measure requiring documentary proof of citizenship when registering to vote, helping ensure that only eligible U.S. citizens participate in our elections.
findings.note: End-of-session report: he describes SB 986 and says it did not pass before adjournment.

findings.passage: While SB 986 advanced through the legislative process this session, it ultimately did not cross the finish line before adjournment.
findings.note: Reports SB 986 did not become law in 2026.

findings.passage: To restore faith and integrity in elections, it is imperative to ensure noncitizens cannot participate.
findings.note: Written in a Senate release; he says he spoke about the SAVE Act and SB 986 on a radio show.

findings.passage: I believe requiring documentary proof of U.S. citizenship for new voter registrations will ensure only eligible Missouri citizens vote and restore full public trust in our elections.
findings.note: His stated reason for requiring documents at new registration.

findings.passage: Protecting the security of elections is one of the basic tenets of the conservative platform and the main reason I filed Senate Bill 152, now one vote in the Missouri House of Representatives away from the governor’s desk.
findings.note: Describes SB 152 as his election-security bill.

findings.passage: The legislation prohibits foreign influence in the initiative petition process and requires a person to show documentary proof of citizenship when they first register to vote.
findings.note: His description of what SB 152 does.

findings.passage: This will enhance election integrity by putting a stop to voting by illegal immigrants, as well as foreign nationals controlling the outcome of constitutional amendments.

I filed Senate Bill 62 to mandate documentary proof of citizenship when registering to vote, require election authorities to perform system maintenance on a quarterly basis and refer cases against those accused of violating election laws directly to the attorney general instead of the designated prosecuting attorney.
findings.note: Describes SB 62: document proof at registration, quarterly voter-roll maintenance, referral of election-law cases to the attorney general.

findings.passage: The second provision of this resolution pertains to non-citizen voting.
findings.note: From his report on SJR 78, which also proposed a ranked choice ban.

findings.passage: It would amend our state constitution to only allow U.S. citizens to vote in our elections.
findings.note: His description of the citizens-only voting provision of SJR 78.

findings.passage: I believe Missouri's current "stand your ground" law that passed in 2016 falls short of protecting Second Amendment rights in cases of self-defense when it comes to the presumption of innocence.
findings.note: In his Senate newsletter, he explains SB 363, which lets a defendant raise a self-defense claim at a pre-trial hearing, and says the 2016 stand-your-ground law does not go far enough.
subjects: gun rights and the Second Amendment

findings.passage: Missouri's "stand your ground" law was passed in 2016, but giving it more teeth could help protect Second Amendment rights and law-abiding gun owners from unmerited cases.
findings.note: In his Senate newsletter, he reports SB 363 passed the Senate transportation and public safety committee on April 7 and describes it as due process for gun owners who defend themselves.
subjects: gun rights and the Second Amendment

findings.passage: House Bill 1175 is now in the Senate and could further solidify second amendment protections into state law. I will keep fighting to pass this bill before adjournment Friday.
findings.note: In his Senate newsletter, under a heading on Second Amendment rights, he backs HB 1175 and notes the 2021 Second Amendment Preservation Act, meant to guard gun owners from federal overreach, is being litigated.
